_experiment.description: Activation function sweep — sigmoid. More severely saturating than tanh: sigmoid maps all inputs to (0,1) and its derivative sigma'(x) = sigma(x)(1-sigma(x)) is at most 0.25. The adjust step gradient is expected to vanish more quickly than for either ReLU or tanh, resulting in the worst sparsity curve of the three activations. The d_manifold evolution plot should show this directly: faster growth = less effective compensation.
literature: Amari 1998 (Natural Gradient): the geometry of the parameter space depends on the activation function through the Fisher information matrix — tanh and ReLU induce different manifold curvatures
Li et al. 2018 (loss landscape visualisation): activation choice strongly affects loss landscape geometry, which governs how the adjust gradient step navigates the manifold
